report: The brain tissue section shows eosinophilic amorphous material, disrupted architecture, and reduced cellularity, indicative of necrosis or proteinaceous deposits. Hyperchromatic nuclei suggest reactive or inflammatory cells, with mild perivascular cuffing. No malignant cells are evident. These findings suggest potential inflammation, infection, or ischemic injury, but specific diagnosis requires further clinical correlation and testing.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Histologic features of herpes simplex virus esophagitis
evidence.text: HSV esophagitis can show ulceration, necrotic debris, multinucleated giant squamous cells, ground-glass or eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination. Viral immunohistochemistry or another confirmatory method may be needed because viral esophagitis patterns can overlap.

review.assessment: The vision models suggest various malignancies, but the pathology report explicitly denies the presence of malignant cells and describes non-specific necrotic/inflammatory brain tissue.
rationale: The de-identified report explicitly states 'No malignant cells are evident,' contradicting all candidate labels which are malignancies.

Reported findings of 'eosinophilic amorphous material' and 'reduced cellularity' are indicative of necrosis or proteinaceous deposits rather than the hypercellularity required for 'lower-grade glioma' or the glandular structures of adenocarcinomas [PMC:3418538-ColorectalMorphology].
discrepancies: Vision models (CONCH, MUSK, QUILTNET) predicted 'lower-grade glioma', but the report describes necrosis and reduced cellularity rather than the hypercellular glial tissue characteristic of gliomas.
PLIP predicted 'kidney renal clear cell carcinoma', which is unsupported by the report's description of brain tissue.
recommended_review: Neuropathology review to differentiate between ischemic injury, infection, or proteinaceous deposition.
Clinical correlation with imaging and patient history.
limitations: The candidate label list is restricted to malignancies, whereas the pathology report suggests a non-malignant process.
